name: candidate_lane_selection
summary: Single-byte composite player-or-monster target selection. Native configuration and +2916 choose which domain to try first; failure retries the other domain once. Each attempt resets +2582/+2584 and +2612. The player branch runs 0x10864d90 and binds kind 1. The monster branch binds kind 13 and scans up to 40 active, eligible other em records with matching area +2040, normalized ground group +2010, positive life and configured horizontal/vertical bounds. A hit writes its domain-local slot to +2612/+2584. DSL: self.select_target_entity(EntityTarget::PlayerOrMonster).
control_flow: consumes only the opcode; handler returns the incoming continuation cursor after at most two domain attempts
domain_notes: No selector or payload is consumed. The initial domain is configuration-dependent, not always player-first. The result slot must be interpreted together with command kind 1 or 13.
The handler does not synchronize saved +3231/+3232/+3234.

name: set_runtime_flag_40
summary: Sets entity-status word +1042 bit 0x40 and calls 0x113aaac0. The helper reads the actor position and the position of its +1100 object, classifies their spatial relation and dispatches additional processing through 0x113aac50/0x113aae90/0x113ab090. The game meaning of bit 0x40 and the complete helper effect remain unconfirmed; this is not a proven general boolean or collision switch.
control_flow: inline; continue at cursor + 1
writes: additional state affected by 0x113aaac0 and its dispatched helpers
domain_notes: The field is a known entity-status word, but that does not establish a game-level name for bit 0x40. Unlike 0x86, this opcode invokes additional spatial processing.

name: clear_runtime_flag_40
summary: Clears entity-status word +1042 bit 0x40 and consumes the opcode. No helper is called. The game meaning of this bit is unconfirmed; it is not established as a general collision/interaction toggle and is not the inverse of all 0x85 side effects.
control_flow: inline; continue at cursor + 1
domain_notes: Only the bit clear is proved. 0x85 additionally calls 0x113aaac0; clearing the bit does not undo that helper.

name: place_at_species_point
summary: Indexes the species point table through dword_118C5784[10*species] + 12*operand and copies its three f32 coordinates to world position +172/+176/+180 and previous-position snapshot +1784/+1788/+1792. This places the actor directly; it does not merely select an AI target point. The handler does not check the table pointer or index bounds.

operands.meaning: 12-byte point index in the species point table

control_flow: inline handler; returns cursor + 2
domain_notes: This species point table is also used by 0x91 and is distinct from the current-area ground-point target tables. No universal valid index range has been established.

name: face_species_point
summary: Uses the operand to index the same species point table as 0x90. Passes that point in ECX and the current actor world position as the stack argument to 0x10855830, computes the planar heading toward the point, zero-extends the 16-bit result and writes the whole dword +164. Does not move the actor. The handler does not check table/index bounds.

operands.meaning: 12-byte point index in the species point table; not ignored

control_flow: inline handler; returns cursor + 2
domain_notes: Hex-Rays omits the ECX input to 0x10855830 in the current prototype. The operand-indexed point and both position inputs are confirmed by assembly.

control_flow: handler returns a replacement cursor; canonical layout is 94 00 count, repeated 94 01 value/body, optional 94 02 default, 94 03 end
domain_notes: AI table initialization at sub_10860360 sets this shared global to 0. No nonzero writer has been confirmed; its source and any debug/test purpose remain unresolved.

Native scripts use case 0 for normal AI selection and case 1 for 82 03 04 (root[18][4]). This slot performs self.action(3:2, 0) in Fire Dragon tables, binds the current target (0x13) and performs self.action(3:4, 0) in the examined Basarios/Gravios tables, and immediately returns in species-100 tables. The global is neither a universal action id nor the actor's mode byte.

name: set_heading_u8
summary: Writes the entire dword heading +164 to operand << 8. The operand is an absolute heading quantized to 256 steps per full turn, not a delta or degrees. The low eight bits and upper sixteen bits of the stored heading are cleared; no turn interpolation or waiting occurs.

name: scaled_runtime_threshold_gate
summary: Selector 0 enters the body when float(foraging-related meter +2700) <= float(operand byte 2 * f32(0.01) * float(configured base +2712)); a greater value skips to else/end through nested 0x9a blocks. Selector 1 scans to selector 2. This is a direct single-precision comparison with no integer truncation, reading the same meter/base pair replenished by 0x4f. DSL remains native(...).
control_flow: handler cursor replacement; nested terminators are 0x9a selectors 1/2
domain_notes: 0x119B5EF0 is f32 0.01. CVTSI2SS/MULSS/COMISS followed by JNB at 0x1086688E enters the body when the scaled threshold is at least the current meter; unlike 0x21 there is no CVTTSS2SI.

+2700 has foraging-related and species-specific action/mode consumers, as well as a gated zero-value request path through 0x10856170. It is not a fixed cooldown or a proven universal satiety scale; domain remains generic.
